Package gooeypainter

package gooeypainter
GooeyPainter: a Painter that moves around a grid and paints squares, made to work just like the Neighborhood from Code.org's CSA curriculum, but in a real IDE such as VS Code.

Add import gooeypainter.*; to the top of your file and create a Painter. A window showing the grid opens automatically the first time a Painter is made, and every action the Painter takes is animated in it. There is nothing else to set up: no window to create and nothing to start.


 import gooeypainter.*;

 public class MyNeighborhood {
     public static void main(String[] args) {
         // Start at (0, 0), facing east, with 10 units of paint
         Painter artist = new Painter(0, 0, "east", 10);

         artist.paint("red");
         artist.move();
         artist.paint("#FFA500");   // hex codes work too, like ones from pixilart.com
         artist.move();
         artist.paint("gold");

         artist.hidePainter();      // get out of the way so the art shows
     }
 }

Coordinates

Each square has an (x, y) location. (0, 0) is the top-left square. x increases going right (east) and y increases going down (south), the same as on Code.org and in most computer graphics.

            x = 0     x = 1     x = 2
   y = 0  (0, 0)    (1, 0)    (2, 0)        north is up
   y = 1  (0, 1)    (1, 1)    (2, 1)        south is down
   y = 2  (0, 2)    (1, 2)    (2, 2)

Making your own Painter class

A Painter can only turn left. To teach it new tricks, write a class that extends Painter and add your own methods, just like PainterPlus on Code.org:


 import gooeypainter.*;

 public class PainterPlus extends Painter {

     public PainterPlus(int x, int y, String direction, int paint) {
         super(x, y, direction, paint);
     }

     public void turnRight() {
         turnLeft();
         turnLeft();
         turnLeft();
     }
 }

Setting up the grid with grid.txt

The grid is read from a file named grid.txt in your project folder (the folder you opened in VS Code). If there is no grid.txt, you get a blank 16 x 16 grid. Draw the grid one row per line, with y = 0 on the first row, and put spaces between the squares:

  • . is open grass
  • X is an obstacle the Painter can't move into
  • B followed by a number is a paint bucket holding that much paint, such as B5

Lines that start with // are comments. Every row must have the same number of squares. This grid.txt makes a 6 x 4 grid with two buckets and two obstacles:

 // My neighborhood
 .  .  .  .  .  .
 .  B5 .  X  .  .
 .  .  .  X  .  B3
 .  .  .  .  .  .

Colors

paint(String) accepts the same colors as Code.org: any of the 140 standard web color names, such as "red", "skyblue", "darkgreen", or "gold" (capital letters don't matter), or a hex code such as "#FF8800" or "#F80". Hex codes make it easy to use exact colors from a pixel art editor like pixilart.com.

The window

The speed slider at the bottom of the window controls how fast the Painter moves; all the way to the right is instant, which is handy for big pixel art. The Show coordinates box labels every row and column. The status line describes the last thing that happened.

Errors

Some mistakes stop your program, like on Code.org. When that happens, a line starting with [EXCEPTION] is printed, the window's title says STOPPED, and the window stays open so you can see where the Painter was. These mistakes stop the program by throwing a GooeyPainterException:

  • moving off the grid or into an obstacle
  • painting on a square that has a paint bucket
  • using a color or direction that isn't recognized
  • creating a Painter at a location that isn't on the grid
  • a problem in grid.txt

Other mistakes just print a message, and the program keeps going:

  • painting with no paint: "There is no more paint in the painter's bucket"
  • taking paint where there is no bucket: "There is no paint to collect here"
  • scraping a square with no paint: "There's no paint to remove here"

To avoid these, check first with methods like canMove(), hasPaint(), and isOnBucket().
